At Sword, we’re building AI to heal billions and unlock humanity’s full potential. In doing so, we’re pioneering AI Care, a fundamentally new approach to healthcare built for medical reasoning, safety, and real-time treatment, not generic technology applied after the fact. As both a clinical-centric frontier AI lab and an applied AI platform, Sword is reimagining how care is delivered at scale, removing traditional barriers like appointments, waiting rooms, and stigma so more people can access the care they need—and ultimately get back to lives lived in full.

Since 2020, Sword has expanded across physical therapy, women’s health, cardiometabolic, and mental health, and is now moving beyond the session to a fully AI-native, 24/7 care program that brings physical activity, therapeutic exercise, psychotherapy, nutrition, and behavior change into one connected experience. More than 700,000 members across three continents have completed over 10 million AI sessions, helping 1,000+ enterprise clients avoid more than $1 billion in unnecessary healthcare costs. Backed by 42 clinical studies, 44+ patents, and more than $500 million raised from leading investors including Khosla Ventures, General Catalyst, and Founders Fund, Sword is defining a new standard for healthcare.

AI Proficiency at Sword

AI fluency is a core expectation at Sword. Every candidate is assessed against our three-level framework — be ready to share real examples of how AI is already part of how you work.

  • Explorer (Level 1) — Uses AI daily to boost personal productivity

  • Builder (Level 2) — Creates workflows and tools that elevate the whole team

  • Integrator (Level 3) — Embeds AI into products and processes at scale

Every hire must demonstrate at least Level 1. The expected level will vary depending on the seniority of the role.

Role

We are hiring a Physiotherapist (PT), based in Portugal, motivated by delivering the best possible patient care. This PT will join our team and will work remotely within Portugal! If you'd like to be a part of what we're building, please apply.

What you’ll be doing

  • Provide 1-to-1 support to patients through message-based chat and phone/video calls;
  • Apply our digital approach to the assessment and management of patients with women pelvic health disorders;
  • Support the clinical validation of new therapeutic programs and products by assisting in data collection and testing.

What you need to have

  • Must have a Bachelor’s degree in Physiotherapy;
  • Completion of additional formal pelvic health education course(s), such as level 1 pelvic coursework (or equivalent);
  • A minimum of 3 years of clinical experience in the treatment of pelvic health disorders;
  • A passion for personalised care that recognises the whole person, and views good health as more than just the absence of disease;
  • Excellent interpersonal skills that come across even through a digital care workspace, translating in the ability to engage our patients;
  • Ability to balance clinical responsibilities with a strong focus on member empowerment, behavioral change, and motivational engagement;
  • Hard-working and able to handle the pressure of a fast-paced environment;
  • A strong commitment to data security and privacy.

*The range below reflects base, variable, and equity for this role.

This is a starting point, not a ceiling — once someone joins and proves they're outlier talent, we adjust quickly to make sure their compensation matches their impact.

The range reflects base salary plus any variable, bonus, or sales incentives, and our estimate of the value of private company stock options where applicable. It's subject to change, and future stock value isn't guaranteed. Sword also offers additional benefits beyond total compensation.

raw.description:
SRA’s mission is to level up every day to protect our clients and their customers. This begins with our team members and their experience. SRA prides itself on maintaining a culture where team members have a shared sense of support and belonging, consistent with our It’s Personal company value. At SRA, we prioritize transparent career pathing, varied DEI programming and community groups, competitive benefits including mental health support, and an emphasis on a sustainable, healthy, and engaging work culture. SRA has twice been named a Best Place to Work by the Philadelphia Business Journal. 

 

These Essential Functions, Requirements, and Skills are guidelines. If you are a candidate who does not meet this exact job description but can demonstrate excellent organization, attention to detail, professionalism, flexibility, and self-direction in your professional background, we hope you apply. SRA values a diverse workplace and strongly encourages women, people of color, LGBTQ+ individuals, people with disabilities, members of ethnic minorities, and veterans to apply. 

Summary/Objective 

The Cybersecurity Operations Consultant is an entry-level role on Security Risk Advisors’ CyberSOC team. You will help monitor, triage, and investigate security alerts across endpoint, network, identity, and cloud data sources, and you will document and communicate findings suitable for client consumption. This role supports 24x7 SOC operations and provides exposure to multiple client environments, modern security tooling, and structured mentorship and training.

Requirements

Essential Functions 

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. 

  • Continuously monitor and triage security alerts across endpoint, network, identity, and cloud telemetry.
  • Investigate alerts to determine severity, scope, and whether activity is benign, suspicious, or malicious; escalate per documented procedures.
  • Perform initial incident response support activities such as evidence collection, timeline development, and basic containment recommendations under supervision.
  • Use SIEM, EDR, NDR/NSM, and SOAR platforms to detect, investigate, and respond to threats; examples include Splunk or Microsoft Sentinel (SIEM), CrowdStrike Falcon or Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (EDR).
  • Leverage threat intelligence and common frameworks (e.g., MITRE ATT&CK) to enrich investigations and communicate attacker behavior clearly.
  • Thoroughly document work in case management systems, including investigation steps taken, evidence reviewed, decisions made, and recommended next actions.
  • Communicate status and findings to internal leadership and clients with professionalism and clarity (written and verbal).
  • Contribute to continuous improvement by identifying recurring false positives/noisy alerts and providing feedback for tuning and playbook updates.
  • Maintain proficiency through required training, labs, and knowledge sharing; follow policies to protect confidential information.

Supervisory Responsibility 

Not applicable. 

 

Work Environment   

This job operates in a professional office environment or remotely as needed/required. This role routinely uses standard office equipment. 

 

Physical Demands

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk and hear; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; and reach with hands and arms. The employee frequently is required to stand and walk. This is a largely sedentary role.

 

Candidates with disabilities are encouraged to apply and email with any questions. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable disabled individuals to perform the essential functions of this role. 

 

Position Type/Expected Hours of Work

New hires may be assigned to any of our three daily shifts (morning, day, or night) and will work a schedule that includes either Saturday or Sunday. Shifts are assigned based on current coverage needs and resource geolocation. Once assigned, you can expect a consistent shift week to week.

This listing/description is for our team’s Green Shift, which runs from 4:30PM - 1:30AM Eastern.

Required Education and Experience

  • Punctuality and timely attendance to external client and internal stakeholder needs.

 

Preferred Qualifications and Experience

  • Coursework, labs, internship, or work experience in one or more of: incident investigation, digital forensics fundamentals, information security, systems administration, or computer networking.
  • Familiarity with common log sources and security concepts (e.g., authentication logs, Windows event logs, DNS, HTTP, email security).

TITLE:Manager, Government Contracts & ComplianceRESPONSIBLE TO:Assistant General CounselDEPT/LOCATION:LegalSUPERVISES:N/AFLSA STATUS:Exempt

POSITION SUMMARY:

The Government Contracts & Compliance Manager is part of the Legal department and reports to the Assistant General Counsel (AGC). This position leads day-to-day contract administration and compliance for GII, including being responsible for GII’s federal government contracts and subcontracts compliance and nonprofit corporate compliance programs. This positions works closely with Legal, Finance, Procurement, Information Technology/Cybersecurity, Human Resources, the Project Management Office, program teams, and other business owners throughout the organization. The Manager is a self-driven, proactive professional who can interpret complex requirements, build practical processes, maintain audit-ready records, manage multiple deadlines, and communicate clearly with internal and external stakeholders, prime contractors, subcontractors, government representatives, and contractors.

BASIC FUNCTION:

  • Government contract and subcontract administration across the full contract life cycle
  • Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), agency supplement, and contract-clause compliance
  • Compliance program coordination, internal controls, training, monitoring, and audit readiness
  • Subcontractor administration, flow-down management, reporting, and recordkeeping
  • Corporate compliance program administration, including charitable solicitation filings
  • Policies, procedures, training, monitoring and reporting

SPECIFIC DUTIES:

Government Contract Administration

  • Develop and maintain policies, procedures, training materials, compliance calendars, and monitoring tools that support fulfillment of contractual and compliance obligations; coordinate with responsible business owners to track completion of assigned requirements, deliverables, timelines, certifications, and corrective actions, and escalate overdue items, gaps, or compliance risks as appropriate.
  • Administer federal contracts and subcontracts from pre-award review through closeout, including advising business teams on compliance considerations from[solicitations, proposals,andnegotiationsthroughawards,]modifications, deliverables, options, notices, and required certifications.
  • Review and, with the oversight of internal and external legal counsel, interpret contract terms, applicable FAR/DFAR and applicable agency supplement clauses, statements of work, data requirements, and compliance obligations; identify risks and provide practical recommendations to the AGC and business owners.
  • Develop and maintain complete, accurate, and audit-ready contract files, including executed agreements, modifications, correspondence, approvals, deliverables, certifications, subcontract records, and closeout documentation.
  • Create and maintain contract obligation and clause matrices, deliverable calendars, responsibility assignments, and dashboards that provide visibility into deadlines, owners, status, and emerging risks.
  • Coordinate compliance activities across Legal, Finance/Accounting, Procurement, IT/Cybersecurity, Human Resources, PMO, Mission, and program teams, and confirm that assigned obligations are documented and completed.
  • Support government contract and compliance activities involving GII member organizations, including communicating applicable requirements, coordinating required documentation and reporting, tracking member or subcontractor obligations, and escalating identified contractual or compliance issues, while maintainingappropriate distinctionsbetween GII and member responsibilities.
  • Support registrations, representations, and recurring submissions associated with government contracting, including SAM.gov and other agency or prime-contractor systems, as applicable.
  • Prepare for and coordinate responses to audits, assessments, monitoring reviews, information requests, and inquiries from government agencies, prime contractors, auditors, and outside counsel.
  • Provide training and day-to-day guidance to contract owners and operational teams on contract requirements, documentation standards, escalation protocols, and prohibited commitments or unauthorized changes.
  • Track regulatory and contractual developments, assess their potential effect on GII operations, and recommend updates to controls, processes, and training.
  • Prepare periodic reports and metrics for Legal and organizational leadership concerning contract status, compliance obligations, findings, corrective actions, and upcoming deadlines.
  • Coordinate with outside counsel and consultants on assigned government contracts and compliance matters, including workplan management and billing review.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Nonprofit Corporate Compliance

  • Develop and maintain a corporate compliance program that includesprocedures, training materials, compliance calendars, and monitoring tools that support fulfillment ofnonprofitorganizationcompliance obligations; coordinate with responsible business owners to track completion of assigned requirements, deliverables, timelines,and corrective actions, and escalate overdue items, gaps, or compliance risks as appropriate.
  • Administer recurring elements of GII’s corporate compliance program, including annual employee and board policy acknowledgements, conflict-of-interest disclosures, compliance certifications, and required follow-up.
  • Coordinate the intake, documentation, review, escalation, and tracking of ethics, whistleblower, and other compliance concerns in accordance with GII policies and established investigation protocols.
  • Maintain compliance records, registers, calendars, and supporting documentation relating to conflicts of interest, related-party matters, policy acknowledgements, investigations, corrective actions, and required reporting.
  • Support periodic review and implementation of corporate compliance policies, including conflicts of interest, whistleblower and non-retaliation, records retention and destruction, gifts and ethics, and other governance or employee compliance policies.
  • Coordinate annual compliance training and policy distribution; monitor completion; follow up on exceptions; and maintain evidence of completion.
  • Support Legal, Finance, Human Resources, Internal Audit, and Board Relations in gathering and validating governance and compliance information required forannual corporate reports,state charitable registrations, board and committee reporting, and other organizational disclosures.
  • Monitor compliance with records retention requirements and legal hold instructions; assist business owners with retention questions, exception tracking, and periodic compliance reviews.
  • Prepare periodic compliance dashboards and reports identifying training completion, exception trends, open disclosures, investigations, corrective actions, policy reviews, and overdue items.

RELATIONSHIPS:

  • Internal: Work closely with the Legal team and with Finance/Accounting, Procurement, IT/Cybersecurity, Human Resources, PMO, Mission, program teams, Internal Audit, and other GII business owners.
  • GII Members: Contact with member organizations may be required in connection with subcontracting, data, reporting, monitoring, and compliance support.
  • External: Contact with prime contractors, subcontractors, consultants, outside counsel, auditors, vendors, and federal or state governmental agencies.

SKILLS NEEDED:

  • Strong knowledge of federal government contracting principles, contract administration, and regulatory compliance, including experience interpreting FAR/DFAR clauses and agency supplements.
  • Excellent organizational and project-management skills, including the ability to maintain contract files, manage calendars, track multiple dependencies and deadlines, and follow issues through resolution.
  • Strong analytical judgment and risk-identification skills, with the ability to translate complex requirements into clear operational actions.
  • Excellent research, writing, negotiation, and verbal communication skills for both legal and non-legal audiences.
  • High attention to detail while meeting deadlines in a fast-paced, cross-functional environment.
  • Ability to build collaborative relationships and work effectively with people at all levels of the organization.
  • Technology proficiency, including Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, SharePoint, and contract or project management systems; ability to create trackers, dashboards, and structured reports.
  • Sound discretion in handling confidential, proprietary, controlled, or sensitive information.
  • Ability to exercise independent judgment, recognize when escalation is required, and provide well-supported recommendations.

EDUCATION:

Bachelor's degree in business, public administration, finance, law, or a related field. An advanced degree or relevant professional certification,such as CPCM, CFCM, CCCM, CCEP, or CHCis preferred.

EXPERIENCE:

Minimum five years of progressively responsible experience in federal government contract or subcontract administration, corporate compliance, or a closely related field, including substantive experience interpreting and applying federal procurement regulations and contract requirements. Experience supporting federal contracts, nonprofit organizations, federal grantees, or professional-services organizations preferred.

DECISION MAKING:

Make day-to-day decisions regarding contract administration priorities, documentation, monitoring, process implementation, and operational follow-up; identify and escalate material legal, compliance, financial, cybersecurity, performance, and reputational risks; and make sound, supported recommendations to the AGC and other leaders, as appropriate.

SUPERVISION:

N/A

PHYSICAL EFFORT:

Sedentary, lifting 10 lbs. maximum. Walking or standing is required only occasionally. Requires long hours at a computer.

raw.description:
NVIDIA’s accelerated computing platform is foundational to modern HPC and AI. At the center of this platform are CUDA Core Libraries that enable developers to build fast, reliable, and scalable GPU-accelerated software. We are hiring a Senior Software Engineer to develop the Rust experience for CUDA Core Libraries. You will design safe, idiomatic Rust APIs for GPU computing while integrating closely with native C/C++ components. You will join the team building the foundational libraries, algorithms, and language/runtime infrastructure that make CUDA a speed-of-light experience for developers and AI coding agents alike.


What you’ll be doing:

  • Design and implement idiomatic Rust libraries and APIs for foundational CUDA functionality and GPU algorithms.
  • Build safe Rust abstractions over native CUDA and C/C++ interfaces.
  • Develop and maintain the C/C++ components required to support Rust-facing functionality.
  • Establish safe and efficient interoperability between Rust and C/C++, including interfaces that support downstream Python integration.
  • Optimize performance across Rust, native C/C++, and GPU execution boundaries.
  • Own features end-to-end: design, implementation, testing, profiling, benchmarking, documentation, packaging, release, and maintenance.
  • Improve the Rust developer experience through examples, diagnostics, build integration, compatibility testing, CI, and collaboration with C/C++, Python, compiler, and runtime engineers.
  • Work with users to investigate and resolve issues related to safety, correctness, usability, compatibility, and performance.

What we need to see:

  • BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or related field, or equivalent experience.
  • 12 + years of relevant software development experience.
  • Strong production programming skills in Rust and C/C++, with deep understanding of Rust ownership, lifetimes, traits, generics, concurrency, and unsafe code.
  • Experience developing systems libraries, runtime components, and developer-facing APIs.
  • Practical knowledge of foreign-function interfaces and integrating Rust with C/C++ software.
  • Solid understanding of systems software concepts, including performance, concurrency, and API design.
  • Experience with parallel, heterogeneous, or GPU programming.
  • Experience contributing to production or open-source software, including testing, profiling, benchmarking, packaging, and code review.
  • Ability to work independently, define scope, and drive complex projects to completion.
  • Strong written communication skills and ability to work effectively in large, multi-language codebases (Rust, C/C++, build systems, toolchains, CI).

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Strong understanding of CPU/GPU architecture and performance optimization, with hands-on experience in GPU-accelerated stacks (CUDA C++/Python, PyTorch, JAX, Numba, CuPy, or similar).
  • Proficiency with modern C++ and GPU libraries such as Thrust, CUB, and libcudacxx.
  • Experience with compiler infrastructure and tooling, including LLVM, Clang, or MLIR.
  • Experience designing safe Rust abstractions over low-level or asynchronous systems, including exposure to Python interoperability.
  • Demonstrated interest in developer tools, library design, and improving developer productivity
Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and the pay of employees in similar positions. The base salary range is 224,000 USD - 356,500 USD for Level 5, and 272,000 USD - 431,250 USD for Level 6.

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.

About Doit

We are focused on reinventing how people spend, save, invest, exchange, travel, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and become an expert at ease. We believe AI will help make finance smart, assessible and safe.

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future for our society.

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

The Role

We are looking for product owners to own product areas within Doit's AI Finance.

This role is for builders who can understand users, define product direction, work with engineering and design, launch fast and keep improving after release.

What You'll Own

  • Own product areas across insurance, payments, savings, investing, travel or other financial services.

  • Define user problems, product scope, success metrics, roadmap and launch plans.

  • Work with engineering, design, data, operations, compliance and business teams.

  • Turn complex financial products into simple, usable customer journeys.

  • Use data, feedback, research and production issues to improve product decisions.

  • Launch features, monitor performance and drive iterations.

  • Make trade-offs between speed, user experience, business impact, compliance and operational complexity.

What We're Looking For

  • Experience as Product Manager, Product Owner, founder, growth/product operator or similar role.

  • Strong product sense and ability to simplify complex workflows.

  • Able to work with engineers and designers to ship real products.

  • Comfortable with metrics, user feedback, experiments and post-launch learning.

  • Strong writing, prioritization and stakeholder management.

  • High ownership and ability to drive work with limited guidance.

  • Experience in fintech, insurance, payments, consumer apps or high-growth products is a strong advantage.

The Kind of Builder We Want

  • Starts from user problems, not feature lists.

  • Can make decisions with incomplete information.

  • Knows how to ship quickly and learn after launch.

  • Works well with engineering without hiding behind process.

  • Honest about what changed because of their work versus wider team effort.

This Role Is Not For

  • People who only write decks and do not drive execution.

  • PMs who cannot work deeply with engineering.

  • Candidates who need perfect data before making decisions.

  • People who launch features and then stop caring.

  • PMs who exaggerate business impact without understanding attribution.

Location

This role is based in Malaysia. This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our Malaysia office at least 3 days per week.

1. Online assessment or practical task

raw.excerpt: Are you ready to unlock intelligence? If you don’t think you meet all of the criteria below but are still interested in the job, please apply.
raw.description:
Are you ready to unlock intelligence?

If you don’t think you meet all of the criteria below but are still interested in the job, please apply. Nobody checks every box - we’re looking for candidates that are particularly strong in a few areas, and have some interest and capabilities in others.

About the Role:
Kong is the AI Connectivity Company. We build the infrastructure that lets enterprises govern APIs and AI traffic at scale — and that infrastructure is becoming critical to how India's government and public sector modernize their systems.
We're hiring an Account Executive to own a defined patch of PSU (Public Sector Undertaking) and Government accounts across India. You'll work the full government buying cycle — tenders, GeM listings, System Integrator relationships, empanelment — to bring Kong's platform into major public-sector modernization programs.

This role is based in Delhi and reports to a Country Manager.

What You'll Do:

  • Own the sales cycle, government-style. Lead deals from first conversation through RFP response, technical and financial bid submission, and contract award. Track PQ (pre-qualification) criteria, EMD requirements, and L1 bidding dynamics. Keep your pipeline accurate to what's actually documented in the tender process — not what looks good in a forecast.

  • Work the ecosystem, not just the account. Government and PSU deals rarely close direct. Build real relationships with the System Integrators (SIs) and OEM partners who carry the technical bid, and make sure Kong is positioned — and empanelled — before the tender drops.

  • Navigate multiple stakeholders. IT Secretaries, CTOs and CIOs at PSUs, nodal officers, procurement and finance committees — each has different priorities and a different definition of "done." Map them accurately and plan around all of them.

  • Build account plans for your patch. Identify which departments and PSUs are actively modernizing, where their budget cycles sit, and what a realistic path to close looks like. Then execute against it.

  • Get fluent in the platform and the landscape. Know Kong's API and AI governance platform well enough to defend it in a technical bid, and know where competitors are already empanelled.

  • Meet your number. Consistently hit quota. Government cycles are long — consistency across quarters matters more than any single deal.

  • Bring in the rest of Kong early. Loop in sales engineering, legal, and the channel team before compliance and certification requirements (STQC, data residency, MeitY empanelment) become a bottleneck late in the deal.

  • Travel. Expect real time in government offices and PSU sites across India. This is a relationship business, and relationships in this sector are built in person.

What You'll Bring:

  • 8-12 years in B2B SaaS or enterprise technology sales, with direct experience selling into Indian government departments or PSUs. This isn't optional — the public-sector buying process is different enough that generalist enterprise experience alone won't carry you.

  • A track record of consistently hitting quota (typically in the ₹2–5 Cr / $300K–$750K range) sold through longer, multi-stakeholder government cycles.

  • Working knowledge of India's government tendering lifecycle — GeM, RFP/RFI processes, technical and financial bids, PQ criteria, EMD — and how empanelment with bodies like MeitY or NIC actually works in practice.

  • Established relationships with System Integrators and OEM partners active in India's public-sector technology space.

  • Process discipline and patience. Government deals move on their own timeline. You bring structure to that timeline — you don't try to force it.

  • Executive presence with senior government officials and PSU leadership, along with the judgment to know when to push and when to wait.

  • Ownership with collaboration. You run your patch, but you know when to pull in your manager, sales engineering, or a partner. In the public sector, this isn't a solo sport.

About Kong:

Kong Inc., the AI Connectivity Company, is building the connectivity layer of AI. Trusted by the Fortune 500® and AI-native startups alike, Kong’s unified API and AI platform enables organizations to secure, manage, accelerate, govern, and monetize the flow of intelligence across APIs and AI traffic — on any model, any cloud. For more information, visit .

raw.excerpt: About CoalfireCoalfire is on a mission to make the world a safer place by solving our clients’ hardest cybersecurity challenges.
raw.description:
About Coalfire

Coalfire is on a mission to make the world a safer place by solving our clients’ hardest cybersecurity challenges. We work at the cutting edge of technology to advise, assess, automate, and ultimately help companies navigate the ever-changing cybersecurity landscape. We are headquartered in Chicago, Illinois with offices across the U.S. and U.K., and we support clients around the world.
But that’s not who we are – that’s just what we do.
We are thought leaders, consultants, and cybersecurity experts, but above all else, we are a team of passionate problem-solvers who are hungry to learn, grow, and make a difference.

Position Summary

Coalfire is looking for a dynamic, results-driven Enterprise Account Executive to drive growth within strategic accounts and spearhead new client acquisition efforts. In this role, you’ll own a portfolio of enterprise clients, with a focus on expanding and protecting Coalfire’s Compliance Audit and Advisory services. You'll operate with a hunter mindset—navigating complex buying cycles, building executive relationships, and driving revenue across existing and net-new logos.

The Account Executive operates with a hunter mindset and serves as a consultative partner to client executives with a focus on enterprise, mid-market, or emerging accounts depending on team assignement. The role requires the ability to navigate complex buying cycles, understand business and cybersecurity priorities, position the right Coalfire solutions, and lead opportunities from initial discovery through proposal, negotiation, close, and follow-on growth. Success depends on strong executive relationships, disciplined account planning, accurate forecasting, and effective collaboration with cross-functional teams.

What You'll Do

    New Business Development:

  • Create and execute quarterly business development plans that align with Coalfire’s current and future cybersecurity portfolio and revenue goals.
  • Generate,qualify, and progress pipeline through outbound prospecting, targeted demand-generation activities, referrals, and inbound leads.
  • Develop and execute multi-touch, consultative sales strategies tailored to client priorities, stakeholders, and buying processes.
  • Pursue new logos and develop business with new buyers and business units within existing accounts.
  • Coordinate the resources required to identify, qualify, advance, and secure opportunities.

    • Account Growth, Retention, and Strategy:

  • Manage a defined set of strategic accounts and prospects, maintaining clear account strategies, stakeholder maps, opportunity priorities, and account plans.
  • Build trusted, long-term relationships with client executives and key decision-makers, including C-suite, business, technology, cybersecurity, risk, and compliance leaders.
  • Identify and pursue expansion, upsell, cross-sell, renewal, and follow-on opportunities across Coalfire services and capabilities.
  • Understand evolving client needs and position solutions that support the client’s business, cybersecurity, compliance, and risk objectives.
  • Maintain customer strategy and direction while coordinating account activity across internal teams.

    • Sales Strategy & Execution:

  • Drive the full sales cycle from discovery and solution positioning through proposal development, pricing, negotiation, close, and transition to delivery.
  • Lead or coordinate account pursuits, including client procurement, proposal development, Statement of Work development, pricing strategy, contract negotiation, and risk management.
  • Establish and follow repeatable processesusing MEDDPICCmethodology for lead qualification, deal review, approval, pipeline progression, and deal execution.
  • Organize and lead pursuit teams and ensure opportunities advance with the appropriate resources, decisions, and next steps.
  • Lead client-facing security strategy, planning, workshop, and formal proposal sessions as appropriate to the opportunity.

    • Client Engagement & Advisory:

  • Serve as a trusted advisor in strategic discussions related to cybersecurity, compliance, IT strategy, technology risk, and industry priorities.
  • Communicate complex services and solutions clearly to technical, product, infrastructure and business owners.
  • Lead executive-level presentations, workshops, proposal meetings, and other high-value client engagements.
  • Stay current on cybersecurity market trends, regulatory developments, emerging technologies, industry participants, and evolving business models.
  • Contribute to problem-solving sessions with client representatives, consulting teams, project managers, delivery teams, and other subject-matter experts.

    • Cross-Functional Collaboration:

  • Partner effectively with sales operations, sales solutions team, delivery, project management, marketing, legal, and other internal teams.
  • Coordinate resources to deliver a connected, professional buyer experience.
  • Build market awareness for Coalfire’s cybersecurity portfolio both internally and externally.
  • Provide timely context, feedback, and client intelligence to teams supporting solution development, delivery, and go-to-market activities.

    • Sales Operations and Forecasting

  • Maintain accurate opportunity, pipeline, account, activity, and forecast data in Salesforce and other approved sales tools.
  • Demonstrate forecast accuracy, disciplined pipeline management, and consistent progression of qualified opportunities.
  • Prepare and present quarterly business reviews, account updates, prospect reviews, and market assessments to sales leadership.
  • Track performance against assigned quota, bookings, revenue, renewal, and other team-specific objectives.

What You'll Bring

  • Six or more years of successful experience in direct B2B sales or account management, preferably in cybersecurity, professional services, technology consulting, compliance, or a related environment.
  • Demonstrated success achieving or exceeding quota, bookings, or revenue targets, with a consistent history of pipeline generation and forecast accuracy.
  • Proven experience with hunting and farming, both new-logo acquisition and account expansion in enterprise, mid-market, or strategic accounts.
  • Experience selling complex solutions through long or multi-stakeholder buying cycles.
  • Demonstrated ability to build and lead relationships with C-suite and senior business, technology, cybersecurity, risk, or compliance stakeholders.
  • Strong consultative selling, strategic planning, account planning, negotiation, presentation, verbal, written, and closing skills.
  • Strong strategic thinking, analytical ability, leadership, judgment, and critical-thinking skills.
  • Ability to understand complex technology, services, strategy, and business objectives and translate them into compelling client solutions.
  • Ability to solve complex problems, remove obstacles diplomatically, and work with limited supervision.
  • Proficiency with Salesforce and other sales productivity tools.
  • Bachelor’s degree (four-year college or university) or equivalent combination of education and work experience
  • Must be able to travel up to 50%

Bonus Points

  • Experience selling cybersecurity consulting, managed services, professional services, compliance, GRC, cloud security, IT risk management, or related solutions.
  • Knowledge of cybersecurity frameworks and standards such as FedRAMP, PCI, SOC, ISO, HIPAA, or HITRUST.
  • Established relationships with C-level decision-makers and relevant industry networks.
  • Experience using sales methodologies or frameworks such as Solution Selling, Force Management, or MEDDPICC.
  • Relevant certifications such as CCSK.
  • Experience with ZoomInfo, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Outreach, or comparable sales and prospecting platforms.
  • Experience working in a high-growth, fast-paced consulting or services environment

Why You’ll Want to Join Us

At Coalfire, you’ll find the support you need to thrive personally and professionally. In many cases, we provide a flexible work model that empowers you to choose when and where you’ll work most effectively – whether you’re at home or an office.
Regardless of location, you’ll experience a company that prioritizes connection and wellbeing and be part of a team where people care about each other and our communities. You’ll have opportunities to join employee resource groups, participate in in-person and virtual events, and more. And you’ll enjoy competitive perks and benefits to support you and your family, like paid parental leave, flexible time off, certification and training reimbursement, digital mental health and wellbeing support membership, and comprehensive insurance options.
At Coalfire, equal opportunity and pay equity is integral to the way we do business. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran. Coalfire is committed to providing access, equal opportunity, and reasonable accommodation for individuals with disabilities in employment, its services, programs, and activities. To request reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, contact our Human Resources team at .

Job Description

Software Technical Support Tier 2

About the Role

The Software Technical Support Tier 2 team provides advanced technical assistance to merchants and internal support teams within Elavon. This role serves as an escalation point for more complex technical issues and provides consultative support to Tier 1 and other support teams.

The team currently supports Converge while expanding its knowledge and support of EPG (Elavon Payment Gateway), which is becoming an increasingly important part of Elavon's payment technology environment.

This opportunity is well suited for someone who enjoys solving technical problems but also understands that great technical support requires great customer service. The ideal candidate can investigate an issue, communicate clearly with the customer, and make a complicated technical situation easier to understand.


What You'll Do

  • Provide Tier 2 technical support and troubleshooting for merchants experiencing technical issues.
  • Serve as an escalation resource for STS Tier 1 and provide technical consultations to other internal support teams.
  • Troubleshoot issues involving Converge, payment technology, POS systems, and merchant terminals.
  • Support merchants and internal partners through phone, email, and chat channels.
  • Handle escalated merchant interactions requiring additional technical expertise.
  • Research and troubleshoot issues while clearly communicating solutions and next steps.
  • Continue developing knowledge of EPG (Elavon Payment Gateway) as the organization expands its use of the platform. The position is currently approximately 70% phone-based, with the remaining time divided between chat and email/project work.

What We're Looking For

We're looking for candidates who bring a combination of technical troubleshooting ability and strong customer service skills. Technical knowledge is important, but equally important is the ability to communicate effectively with customers who may be dealing with complicated or frustrating technical issues.

Relevant experience may include:

  • Technical support or advanced troubleshooting experience
  • Experience supporting technology directly with customers
  • POS system or payment-terminal troubleshooting
  • Merchant services or payment-processing experience
  • Payment gateway experience
  • Converge experience
  • Experience in technical customer-support environments where both technical proficiency and customer service are emphasized
  • Computer science education or other demonstrated technical learning/development

Candidates do not need to arrive fully trained on EPG. Prior awareness or familiarity with the platform would be valuable, but the manager specifically noted that even the existing team is still developing its EPG expertise.


What Will Help You Stand Out

Strong candidates will be able to demonstrate:

  • Genuine hands-on technical troubleshooting experience
  • The ability to diagnose issues rather than simply follow standard customer-service processes
  • Strong verbal communication and customer-service skills
  • Experience troubleshooting POS systems, merchant terminals, payment technology, or similar technical products
  • Exposure to merchant services, payment processing, gateways, or Converge
  • An interest in continuing to grow technically and learn new platforms

Experience in technical customer-support environments such as Apple was specifically identified during the intake as a strong transferable background because of the combination of technical troubleshooting and customer-service expectations.


Schedule

Regular schedule:

Monday-Friday, 12:30 PM - 9:00 PM Eastern Time.

Training schedule:

Monday-Friday, 8:30 AM-5:00 PM Eastern Time. The length of training was not established during the intake.

Work Location

This position was discussed as fully remote. The requisition currently identifies Mississippi, Arizona, Colorado, and Tennessee, although the manager indicated that the recruiting search does not need to be limited specifically to those locations.

If there’s anything we can do to accommodate a disability during any portion of the application or hiring process, please refer to our disability accommodations for applicants.

Benefits:

Our approach to benefits and total rewards considers our team members’ whole selves and what may be needed to thrive in and outside work. That's why our benefits are designed to help you and your family boost your health, protect your financial security and give you peace of mind. Our benefits include the following:

  • Healthcare (medical, dental, vision)

  • Basic term and optional term life insurance

  • Short-term and long-term disability

  • Pregnancy disability and parental leave

  • 401(k) and employer-funded retirement plan

  • Paid vacation (from two to five weeks depending on salary grade and tenure)

  • Up to 11 paid holiday opportunities

  • Adoption assistance

  • Sick and Safe Leave accruals of one hour for every 30 worked, up to 80 hours per calendar year unless otherwise provided by law

Review our full benefits available by employment status here.

Camunda is the enterprise platform for agentic orchestration , enabling organizations to coordinate AI agents, people, and systems across complex, end-to-end business processes. With built-in governance, auditability, and human oversight, Camunda gives enterprises the control they need to move AI from pilots to production — safely and at scale. Trusted by over 700 organizations worldwide , including 9 of top 10 US banks, Camunda helps enterprises boost operational efficiency, accelerate time-to-value, and deliver better customer experiences.

Fully remote and global, we are in the middle of something bigger: transforming into an AI-first organisation, built on our own platform . We use Agentic AI to automate, orchestrate intelligent processes, and elevate human contribution across every team.

Named GP Bullhound’s Top 100 Next Unicorn list, 2025 Great Place to Work certified.Visionary in 2025 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Business Orchestration and Automation Technologies. ranked 3rd in Flexa's 2026Most Flexible Companies , We’re growing fast and looking for top talent to join our team. If you want meaningful work, visible impact and put something genuinely rare on your CV, keep reading. About The Role ProcessOS is a new kind of Camunda product: business processes described in natural language, generated as executable BPMN workflows, and improved autonomously from production data. We’re hiring the first cohort of Forward Deployed Engineers to bring it into production at enterprise customers. You’ll own the deployment journey from first process file to a working, improving system, and hand off a functioning capability to the customer’s team. The code you write and the patterns you discover feed directly back into how ProcessOS is built. This is a rare opportunity to shape a product, a function, and a field practice from day one.

You’ll work end‑to‑end across Java services and React interfaces, collaborating closely with a talented global team to measure, improve, and scale performance and fault tolerance in real-world distributed systems.

Curious about the kind of challenges you'll work on at Camunda? Watch this quick30-minute talkfrom our engineers to learn more about the new Camunda Exporter and how we’re solving complex problems at scale What You’ll Be Doing
  • Deploy and prove: own the end-to-end journey from first process file to a running, measurably improving production workflow.
    • At 90 days: at least one workflow running, the improvement loop active, and measurable fitness gains the customer can see.
    • At 12 months: 3–5 customers with viable deployments.
  • Feed the product: You're building the product as you work with customers; this includes features, agents, and skill files. When you find a bug, you're empowered to fix it.
  • Drive organisational adoption: work across technical and business stakeholders to turn early deployments into lasting customer capability
  • Work at technical depth: configure Camunda clusters, debug integration failures, and build custom agents where platform defaults don’t fit
  • Build the playbook: document what good looks like as you discover it and make the next deployment faster
  • Hand off deliberately: leave each customer team trained, independent, and able to act on improvement results without you
What You Bring
  • Enterprise production experience: you’ve shipped something inside a large organisation and stayed to see it operate. You know why governance and resilience matter at scale.
  • Technical depth: you can debug an integration failure, write a custom agent against a legacy API, stand up a Camunda cluster from scratch, and explain generated BPMN to both engineers and business leads.
  • Stakeholder communication: you work effectively across engineering, architecture, and business leadership and adapt how you communicate without losing precision.
  • Practical AI experience: you’ve used AI to solve real problems in production – not just experimented. You understand context management, prompt engineering, agent testing, and integration tradeoffs.
  • Comfort with ambiguity: you make sound judgment calls without a playbook and document what you learn.
  • Occasional travel may be required
  • Ability and/or willingness to use our product
Nice-to-haves
  • Experience in a customer-facing engineering or professional services role.
  • Familiarity with regulated industries such as financial services, healthcare, or insurance
  • Production experience with agentic systems or AI-integrated workflows.
  • Contributions to a shared platform or open source project that others built on.

Position Overview

Power your future with Qualus as a Principal Consultant on our Advanced Grid Solutions team. The Principal Consultant is a senior client-facing leader within the Advanced Grid Solutions Team, providing technical and consulting leadership for complex grid modernization initiatives. The role combines deep utility and advanced grid expertise with strategic advisory, solution architecture, systems integration, and delivery leadership to help utilities evaluate, adopt, and integrate emerging grid technologies.

Advanced grid initiatives often involve evolving technologies, requirements, and operating models. The Principal Consultant is expected to work effectively in these environments, bring structure to complex or ambiguous challenges, and develop practical solutions that can be implemented and supported. The role works across utility operations, engineering, IT, OT, technology vendors, and Qualus delivery teams to guide solutions from strategy and architecture through implementation and operational readiness.

Responsibilities

Advanced Grid Solutions:

  • Lead advanced grid and emerging utility technology initiatives, including AMI, EMS, DERMS, ADMS, DER integration, and flexible interconnections.
  • Bring deep grid-domain experience to help utilities address changing operational needs and modernize the grid.
  • Help clients evaluate and apply new technologies to challenges such as DER growth, data center loads, and grid flexibility.
  • Take a vendor-agnostic approach, focusing on the technologies and solutions that best fit the client’s needs.
  • Provide technical leadership and guidance across complex utility programs and client engagements.

System Integration, Architecture & Project Delivery:

  • Lead technical delivery of large, complex grid modernization and systems integration projects.
  • Provide solution architecture expertise, turning utility business and operational needs into practical solutions that can be implemented and supported.
  • Apply strong systems architecture practices to determine how systems, interfaces, data, and technologies should work together.
  • Develop pragmatic architectures based on experience with what works in real-world utility environments.
  • Lead solution design and integration across AMI, EMS, DERMS, ADMS, SCADA, GIS, historians, enterprise systems, and other grid technologies.
  • Guide key architecture and design decisions across clients, vendors, and Qualus delivery teams.
  • Provide technical leadership from early design through integration, testing, deployment, and operational readiness.

Innovation, AI, and R&D:

  • Help identify and develop new solutions for emerging utility and grid challenges.
  • Lead and support R&D initiatives involving new technologies, operating models, and industry needs.
  • Support research and demonstration projects in areas such as data center loads, flexible interconnections, and DER orchestration.
  • Explore practical uses of AI and advanced analytics within grid operations and project delivery.
  • Work with research organizations, utilities, vendors, and broader Qualus teams to develop and test new ideas.
  • Help turn successful research, pilots, and demonstrations into practical solutions that can be applied on client projects.

Organization Development and Growth:

  • Help grow the Advanced Grid Solutions organization, including its capabilities, services, people, and market presence.
  • Build solution architecture as a core capability through mentoring, design reviews, proven approaches, and knowledge sharing.
  • Mentor and develop consultants in grid technologies, architecture, systems integration, and solution delivery.
  • Capture proven architectures, approaches, tools, and lessons learned for reuse across projects.
  • Support recruiting and development of the technical talent needed to grow the practice.
  • Contribute to proposals, client pursuits, solution development, and new service offerings.
  • Build strong relationships across clients, technology vendors, research organizations, and the broader utility industry.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Minimum of 10 years of experience supporting electric utility operational and advanced grid technologies, including AMI/MDM, DERMS, ADMS, SCADA, EMS, or related systems.
  • Within those 10 years, a minimum of 5 years of consulting, systems integration, or professional services experience supporting electric utilities.
  • Experience with large-scale grid modernization, systems integration, or utility technology implementation projects.
  • Experience applying solution or systems architecture practices within complex utility environments.
  • Experience should have been obtained through one or more of the following:
    • Electric utility consulting or systems integration.
    • Utility software vendor implementation, engineering, solution architecture, product management, or professional services.
    • Electric utility engineering, operations, OT, transmission/distribution, or control center organizations.
    • Advanced grid, DER, grid modernization, research, or emerging technology programs.

Benefits & Compensation

Qualus offers a competitive benefits package for eligible employees, which may include Medical, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance, Short- and Long-Term Disability coverage, Retirement Savings Plans (including employer matching where applicable), Flexible Spending and/or Health Spending Accounts, Employee Assistance Programs (EAP), Parental Leave, Paid Time Off, and Company Holidays. Benefits offerings may vary based on position, work location, and eligibility requirements. The compensation range for this position is provided in accordance with applicable laws and market practices. The final base salary offered may vary based on factors including, but not limited to, education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, internal equity, performance, and business needs. Compensation ranges are subject to change at the Company's discretion and as permitted by applicable law.

Company Overview

Qualus is a leading pure-play power solutions firm and innovator at the forefront of power infrastructure transformation, with differentiated capabilities across grid modernization, resiliency, security, and sustainability. The firm partners with utilities, commercial, industrial, data center, and government clients, and renewable and energy storage developers, offering comprehensive solutions through boutique and integrated advisory, planning, engineering, digital solutions, program management, energy efficiency and specialized field services. Qualus also provides software and technology enabled services and develops breakthrough solutions for critical power industry challenges such as distributed and variable resource integration, emergency management, and secure data exchange. The firm has over 2,000 professionals, with offices throughout the U.S. and Canada.

Equal Opportunity Employer

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity. We are committed to providing an inclusive workplace and do not discriminate on any grounds protected by applicable human rights legislation across Canada and the US.

raw.description:
Peraton Overview

Peraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. As the world’s leading mission capability integrator and transformative enterprise IT provider, we deliver trusted, highly differentiated solutions and technologies to protect our nation and allies. Peraton operates at the critical nexus between traditional and nontraditional threats across all domains: land, sea, space, air, and cyberspace. The company serves as a valued partner to essential government agencies and supports every branch of the U.S. armed forces. Each day, our employees do the can’t be done by solving the most daunting challenges facing our customers. Visit peraton.com to learn how we’re keeping people around the world safe and secure.

Responsibilities

Peraton is seeking a Senior Web Developer(UI & API Integration) to lead front-end development and API integration for a federal environmental platform. You will design and implement user interface updates that enable federal users to access new species data for regulatory consultations, ensuring full Section 508 accessibility compliance throughout. This is a fully remote position.

The Department of the Interior (DOI), U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS), and NOAA's National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) have identified a critical gap in the federal government's ability to conduct comprehensive Endangered Species Act (ESA) research. While FWS operates an authoritative web-based platform for managing data for terrestrial and freshwater species, it does not currently include NMFS marine and anadromous species data forcing agencies to rely on separate, manual processes. This program closes that gap by integrating marine and anadromous species data into the existing FWS platform, creating a single, unified experience for all ESA-listed species.

Work Location: Remote

Day to Day Responsibilities:

  • Lead platform user interface updates to display new species data alongside existing species, including habitat designations, listing status, and regulatory requirements
  • Design and implement the updated geographic query interface for marine and coastal query types
  • Develop and integrate authorized API connections between the platform front-end and the cloud data layer
  • Ensure all UI changes comply with Section 508/WCAG 2.0 Level AA accessibility standards, coordinating with QA Engineers for DHS Trusted Tester Methodology accessibility testing
  • Produce Accessibility Conformance Reports (ACRs) using VPAT Version 2.4 Rev 508 for all UI updates
  • Update the consultation package builder front-end to support new content generation and joint agency consultation package assembly
  • Contribute to the IPaC UI and Logic Update Package, delivering all front-end UI components, geographic query interface updates, and consultation package builder enhancements with accompanying VPAT documentation for government review
  • Support the demo environment setup for government demonstrations, ensuring the UI is stable and demo-ready
  • Implement UI updates based on live consultation feedback from production

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree and 5 years of experience, Master’s degree and 3 years of experience, Associate’s degree and 7 years of experience, HS Diploma and 9 years of experience.
  • U.S. Citizenship required; must have the ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust clearance; all work must be performed within the United States.
  • 5 plus years of web development experience with a focus on federal application front-end development.
  • Proficiency in React, Angular, or equivalent modern JavaScript frameworks.
  • Proficiency in HTML5 and CSS3 for accessible, standards-compliant federal web application development.
  • Deep expertise in Section 508/WCAG 2.0 Level AA accessibility standards and DHS Trusted Tester Methodology.
  • Experience producing VPAT 2.4 Rev 508 Accessibility Conformance Reports.
  • Experience developing and integrating REST APIs in federal web applications.
  • Experience with Git or equivalent version control platforms for federal web application code management.
  • Familiarity with federal web development standards and FedRAMP-compliant deployment.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • DHS Certified Trusted Tester certification.
  • Experience with geographic query interface development or GIS web integration.
  • Experience with federal environmental platforms or consultation systems.
  • Experience with Agile/iterative web development on federal programs.

Target Salary Range

$80,000 - $128,000. This represents the typical salary range for this position. Salary is determined by various factors, including but not limited to, the scope and responsibilities of the position, the individual’s experience, education, knowledge, skills, and competencies, as well as geographic location and business and contract considerations. Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay.

raw.description:
Overview

DecisionPoint seeks an Agile Delivery Lead / Scrum Master to lead Agile execution for Team 2 supporting mission applications and integration capabilities under the USMEPCOM ENLIST program. This senior role facilitates planning, daily coordination, backlog refinement, sprint reviews, demonstrations, and retrospectives while maintaining visibility into delivery commitments, impediments, dependencies, risks, and performance.

The Agile Delivery Lead / Scrum Master works closely with Government stakeholders, product owners, mission liaisons, architects, developers, integration engineers, testers, cybersecurity personnel, trainers, platform teams, and external system stakeholders. The position coordinates weekly demonstrations and prepares required Development Sprint Plans, Sprint Summary Reports, delivery metrics, and related program artifacts.

This position is remote, with Chicago-area candidates preferred.

Note: By applying to this position, you acknowledge and consent to having your resume included in an active competitive government contract bid.

Duties & Responsibilities

The Agile Delivery Lead / Scrum Master will:

  • Lead Agile delivery activities for Team 2 supporting mission applications, interfaces, integrations, and related software capabilities.
  • Facilitate sprint planning, daily coordination meetings, backlog-refinement sessions, sprint reviews, demonstrations, and retrospectives.
  • Establish and maintain a predictable Agile delivery cadence aligned with Government priorities and approved program schedules.
  • Partner with product owners, mission liaisons, and technical leads to ensure the backlog is prioritized, refined, and ready for sprint planning.
  • Help the team establish realistic sprint goals and commitments based on priorities, capacity, interface dependencies, and delivery risks.
  • Track sprint commitments, progress, scope changes, impediments, dependencies, risks, decisions, and action items.
  • Identify and escalate delivery impediments and coordinate their resolution with technical leads, Government stakeholders, and supporting teams.
  • Manage cross-team dependencies involving mission applications, system interfaces, APIs, data exchanges, architecture, infrastructure, cybersecurity, testing, training, and releases.
  • Coordinate delivery dependencies with external systems, data providers, mission partners, and other Agile teams.
  • Track interface assumptions, test-environment dependencies, external decisions, and integration-readiness activities.
  • Coordinate weekly demonstrations and ensure completed capabilities are ready for Government and mission-stakeholder review.
  • Capture demonstration feedback, decisions, and resulting backlog or action-item updates.
  • Prepare, maintain, and submit Development Sprint Plans in accordance with program requirements.
  • Prepare Sprint Summary Reports documenting accomplishments, incomplete work, testing, integration outcomes, demonstrations, feedback, risks, dependencies, and planned follow-up.
  • Track and analyze delivery metrics, including sprint predictability, throughput, cycle time, work aging, impediments, defects, and commitment completion.
  • Use delivery data to identify trends, facilitate improvement discussions, and recommend corrective actions.
  • Coordinate with requirements analysts to ensure user stories, interface requirements, data requirements, and acceptance criteria are clear, testable, traceable, and ready for implementation.
  • Coordinate with developers, integration engineers, testers, cybersecurity personnel, and release teams to support secure development, integration, verification, and deployment.
  • Support backlog prioritization and the expedited handling of urgent defects, failed integrations, or security-related changes.
  • Facilitate communication among Team 2, other Agile teams, program leadership, Government representatives, and external integration stakeholders.
  • Maintain Agile boards, delivery dashboards, dependency logs, action logs, decision records, and related program artifacts in approved tools.
  • Support integration planning, release planning, release-readiness reviews, user acceptance activities, and operational-transition coordination.
  • Coach team members and stakeholders on effective Agile practices, collaboration, transparency, accountability, and continuous improvement.
  • Protect the team’s delivery focus while ensuring critical stakeholder needs, integration dependencies, and program commitments are addressed.
  • Provide delivery status, forecasts, risks, and performance information for program reporting and governance activities.
  • Support continuous improvement of Agile delivery and cross-team integration processes across the ENLIST program.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Candidates must possess all the following:

  • An active Secret clearance or higher.
  • A bachelor’s degree in computer science, information technology, software engineering, or a related field, or an equivalent permitted by the applicable labor category.
  • At least ten years of relevant professional experience.
  • Experience facilitating Agile software-delivery teams.
  • Experience managing dependencies across multiple technical teams or workstreams.
  • Experience facilitating sprint planning, daily coordination, backlog refinement, sprint reviews, demonstrations, and retrospectives.
  • Experience tracking sprint commitments, impediments, risks, dependencies, actions, and delivery metrics.
  • Experience working with product owners, technical leads, developers, testers, and Government or business stakeholders.
  • Ability to manage delivery dependencies involving mission applications, interfaces, integrations, data exchanges, or external systems.
  • Ability to prepare clear sprint plans, delivery summaries, metrics, status reports, and executive-level briefings.
  • Ability to identify delivery risks and impediments, coordinate resolution, and communicate impacts to stakeholders.
  • Strong facilitation, leadership, conflict-resolution, analytical, organizational, and communication skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and maintain delivery discipline in a complex, cross-functional software environment.

Preferred Qualifications

The following qualifications are preferred:

  • A Scrum or Agile certification, such as Certified ScrumMaster (CSM), Advanced Certified ScrumMaster (A-CSM), Certified Scrum Professional - ScrumMaster (CSP-SM), Professional Scrum Master (PSM), SAFe Scrum Master, SAFe Release Train Engineer, PMI Agile Certified Practitioner (PMI-ACP), or an equivalent credential.
  • Experience supporting federal or Department of Defense software-development or modernization programs.
  • Experience leading Agile delivery for mission-critical, regulated, or high-availability information systems.
  • Experience supporting military accession processing, personnel processing, or comparable mission workflows.
  • Experience managing delivery involving APIs, external interfaces, data exchanges, system integrations, or multiple application platforms.
  • Experience preparing formal sprint plans, sprint summary reports, Government demonstrations, and contract-delivery artifacts.
  • Experience coordinating delivery across software, architecture, infrastructure, cybersecurity, testing, data, training, and operations teams.
  • Experience with Agile and collaboration tools such as Jira, Azure DevOps, Confluence, SharePoint, or comparable platforms.
  • Experience working in Agile, DevSecOps, or secure software-development environments.
  • Familiarity with requirements traceability, interface control documentation, integration testing, user acceptance testing, release management, and configuration management.
  • Project Management Professional (PMP) certification.

Our Equal Employment Opportunity Policy

  • EEO and Affirmative Action Policy: DecisionPoint Corporation is an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. It is the policy of DecisionPoint Corporation to provide equal employment opportunity in accordance with all applicable Equal Employment Opportunity/Affirmative Action laws, directives and regulations to all employees and qualified applicants without regard to race, ethnicity, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability status, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other protected status under Federal, State or Local laws.
  • Pay Transparency Policy: In accordance with Presidential Executive Order 13665, DecisionPoint Corporation will not discharge or in any other manner discriminate against employees or applicants because they have inquired about, discussed, or disclosed their own pay or the pay of another employee or applicant. However, employees who have access to the compensation information of other employees or applicants as a part of their essential job functions cannot disclose the pay of other employees or applicants to individuals who do not otherwise have access to compensation information, unless the disclosure is (a) in response to a formal complaint or charge, (b) in furtherance of an investigation, proceeding, hearing, or action, including an investigation conducted by the employer, or (c) consistent with the contractor's legal duty to furnish information.
  • Authorization to Share Resume and Personal Information: By expressing your interest and submitting your resume for this position, you authorize DecisionPoint Corporation to share your resume, as well as personal information included on the resume, with its subsidiaries, affiliates and teaming partners for the purpose of considering you for this position and other available positions requiring comparable skills, education and experience. Should DecisionPoint Corporation. or its affiliates and teaming partners wish to initiate pre-employment discussions, you will be asked to complete an employment application and related employment documents.

raw.description:
Senior Backend Engineer - Introducer Tech - DE

Hybrid in London / Remote within the UK

We’re looking for a Senior Backend Engineer

You'll own the Lending API in Germany, which banks, fintechs, brokers, and comparison sites build on to offer iwoca's finance to their customers. You'll decide how it evolves and help build the features that make partners choose iwoca.

The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £5 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The team

Introducer Tech builds the systems that partners in Germany use to refer businesses to iwoca. The aim is to get new partners integrated quickly and to make applying simple for their customers. The team also looks after how partners earn commission.

Its work covers three main areas:

  • The Lending API. Developing the versioned API and the webhooks that keep partners up to date on their customers.

  • The Introducer Portal. Building the web app that German brokers log in to, to submit applications and upload documents.

  • The sign-up journey. Improving how businesses apply and how well they convert, after a partner referral.

The team is growing to have two product managers, who each focus on either the broker or the partner flow, and three engineers across the backend and frontend, including this hire.

The team currently works in sprints, with three stand-ups a week and planning every two weeks. However, there is room to adapt how it works as it grows.

The role

You'll be the senior engineer behind iwoca's broker and partner channels in Germany, from the tools partners integrate with to the internal systems that broker account managers use.

Ownership and autonomy

  • Own the Lending API in Germany end to end, deciding what to build, when to release a new version, when to retire an old one, and what iwoca can promise partners.

  • Own the developer portal and every tool partners use to integrate, from documentation that their developers and coding agents can build from to self-serve testing that needs no help from iwoca.

Impact

  • Ship the features that make partners choose iwoca, starting with pre-qualification, which shows a customer what they could borrow before they apply.

  • Make integration quick and simple, so a partner can go live with few questions and little hand-holding.

  • Automate parts of the broker funnel and the internal CRM that broker account managers use, cutting friction and the lag between a decision and the action that follows, and building agents wherever they help.

Growth trajectory

  • Set the team's technical direction and shape the product and technical roadmap alongside the product manager.

  • Align designs with the UK engineers who share the API, so German requirements shape the design from the start.

  • As well as being hands on, you’ll develop your mentoring and coaching skills. You’ll help lead the team as the most senior engineer.

You'll work with the commercial colleagues who bring in new partners, and join the team's weekly support rotation.

The requirements

Essential:

  • Backend engineering. You've designed and built production backend systems in Python – ideally with Django, though FastAPI or Flask count too. You've used PostgreSQL or another relational database in production, and kept it fast and maintainable.

  • API design. You've built and evolved APIs that other teams or companies depend on, and made the decisions on structure, versioning, and change.

  • Ownership. You've taken work from a commercial problem through to production – scoping the solution, making the trade-offs, and iterating based on how people use it.

  • Mentoring. You've helped other engineers grow through code reviews and design sessions.

  • AI leverage. You've built agentic workflows, or used AI to scale your engineering output beyond what you could deliver alone. You judge when to use it and when not to.

  • Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail to your audience.

Bonus:

  • Partner onboarding. You've helped external developers integrate with an API – through documentation, test environments, or working with them directly.

  • Full-stack. You've contributed to frontend codebases, particularly in React or TypeScript.

  • CI/CD. You've set up or maintained the pipelines that test and release a production service.

  • Measurement. You've used data, metrics, or A/B tests to check whether a change had the effect you intended.

The salary

We expect to pay from £80,000 to £100,000 for this role. But, we’re open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

The culture

At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.

We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them.

The offices

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

  • Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits

  • Flexible working hours.

  • Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

  • A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

  • 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

  • A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

  • Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

  • 3% pension contributions on total earnings.

  • An employee equity incentive scheme.

  • Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

  • Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

  • Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

  • A learning and development budget for everyone.

  • Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.

  • Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

Useful links:

  • iwoca benefits & policies.

  • Interview welcome pack.

Compensation Range: £80K - £100K
